data.narrative:
Magrathea Metals is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Alex Grant and Jacob Brown that has raised over $100M. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 8 private companies and 1 public company in the Climate & Energy sector, including comparable-stage or adjacent ventures such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using the $100M total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, this method implies a valuation of $200M. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting narrow filter thresholds—while 8 companies operate in the sector, too few clustered at similar valuation tiers or stages to produce a reliable median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $170M to $230M, with a median point of $200M. This range reflects the constraints of a single applicable method and sparse narrow peer comparables in the climate and energy frontier-tech space. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.0x step-up multiplier for this specific sector and stage transition, and the absence of tighter peer clustering to validate assumptions about comparable company progression patterns. Additional revenue, unit economics, or technology differentiation data would strengthen conviction in this range.
